title: Newton iteration and multiple roots
terms: Newton method; Newton–Raphson method; tangent-line iteration; simple root; multiple- root convergence; Newton failure; modified Newton method.

exposition.text:
′
Newton’s iteration is x = x − f (x )/f (x ) whenever the denominator is nonzero. It uses the
n+1 n n n
tangent line’s root as the next approximation. For a sufficiently smooth function with a simple
root α and a sufficiently close initial guess, convergence is at least quadratic.
At a root of multiplicity m > 1, ordinary Newton iteration is generally linear with asymptotic
error factor (m − 1)/m. A poor initial point can diverge, cycle, or reach a zero derivative. Thus
quadratic convergence is not guaranteed merely by having a differentiable function or a plausi-
ble starting point.
′
A simple root satisfies f(α) = 0 and f (α) ̸= 0. A root of multiplicity m has local factorization
m
f(x) = (x − α) g(x) with g(α) ̸= 0. When the multiplicity is known, the modified update
′
x = x − mf(x )/f (x ) removes the ordinary linear slowdown and, under the usual local
n+1 n n n
smoothness conditions, restores at least quadratic convergence.

question.text:
3 3
Newton iteration starts at zero for each of f(x) = x − 2x + 2 and g(x) = x − 1. Which pair of
behaviors occurs, respectively?
(A) Both converge quadratically to real roots.
(B) f cycles between zero and one; the first update for g is undefined.
(C) The first update for f is undefined; g cycles.
(D) Both first updates are undefined.
(E) f reaches a root in one step; g converges linearly.

solution.text:
′ ′
For f , f(0) = 2 and f (0) = −2 give the next iterate one; f(1) = 1 and f (1) = 1 send
′
it back to zero, repeating a two-cycle. For g, g(0) = −1 but g (0) = 0, so division by the
derivative is impossible at the initial step. Neither failure contradicts a local theorem near
a simple root with a sufficiently close start.
